review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the simp lemmas it relies on in LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/Transvection.lean (spinTransvection_pow, spinTransvection_eq_one_iff, spinTransvection_add and others) and spinGroupBaseChange_spinTransvection in BaseChange.lean. The target adds no simp lemmas of its own. The one finding is an interface gap: simp normalises spinTransvection_pow to an ℕ-smul parameter, while the file's Eichler-line and continuity arguments use field scalars. I did not look for a Mathlib lemma that would replace the cast-and-smul_mem_iff step beyond a grep for nsmul_mem_iff and smul_mem_iff. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about how simp behaves on these goals.

findings.problem: The simp-tagged lemmas `spinTransvection_pow` and `spinTransvection_eq_one_iff` leave the goal as `n.factorial • w ∈ ℚ ∙ u`, with an ℕ-smul. Simp cannot finish this. The proof falls back on a manual `rw`, which undoes the ℕ-smul with `← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℚ`. It then applies `smul_mem_iff` with a hand-cast nonzero side goal. So the simp set has no canonical way to decide whether `n • w` lies on the Eichler line `ℚ ∙ u`. The same ℕ-smul-versus-field-scalar mismatch shows up in `hEn` (line 74), where `Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul` has to be passed to `simp only` to match the ℕ-smul from `spinTransvection_pow` with the `t • wp` parameter. Several fixes would remove the mismatch: a field-scalar form of the power lemma, a ℚ-specific lemma `n • w ∈ K ∙ u ↔ w ∈ K ∙ u` for `n ≠ 0` in characteristic zero, or an `n ≠ 0` iff lemma for `spinTransvection hQ hu huw ^ n = 1`.
findings.proposed_change: In Transvection.lean, next to `spinTransvection_pow`, add a lemma for characteristic-zero `K`. For `hu₀ : u ≠ 0` and `n ≠ 0` it would say `spinTransvection hQ hu huw ^ n = 1 ↔ w ∈ K ∙ u`. Mark it `@[simp]` only if its side conditions can be discharged. Alternatively, add a simp lemma stating `n • w ∈ K ∙ u ↔ w ∈ K ∙ u` for `n ≠ 0`. Then `hne` becomes one `simp` or `rw` plus `n.factorial_ne_zero`, with no casts. A scalar-parameter version, `spinTransvection hQ (w := (n : K) • w) .. = spinTransvection hQ hu huw ^ n`, would also let `hEn` avoid `Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul`.
findings.benefit: Downstream users get a single canonical normal form for powers of a transvection lift. They no longer have to move between ℕ-smul and K-smul by hand. This removes the cast bookkeeping in both `hne` and `hEn`, and the pattern will recur wherever other results use powers of `spinTransvection`.

evidence.excerpt: spinTransvection hQ hu huw ^ n = spinTransvection hQ (w := n • w) hu
spinTransvection hQ hu huw = 1 ↔ w ∈ K ∙ u
